# dsh-tokeneconomizer
English | 简体中文

DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that ports [Microsoft
TokenEconomizer](https://github.com/microsoft/To

kenEconomizer) to DSH: learn
reliable project knowledge from earlier sessions, prune tool definition

s the
model never uses, notice repetitive failure loops, and record the token usage
the harness actu

ever uses, notice repetitive failure loops, and record the token usage
the harness actually reports.

This is an independent open-source port, **not** an official Microsoft
product. See Attribution and

an independent open-source port, **not** an official Microsoft
product. See Attribution and license.
## Why

Coding agents re-learn the same repository facts, re-send the same unused tool
schemas, and repeat t

he same failing edits across sessions. TokenEconomizer
found that learning across a repository's ses

sions reduces cost without changing
the agent. This plugin brings the same four mechanisms to DSH:
| Mechanism | What it does here |
| **Micro-skills** | Learns durable project facts from repeated failure -> success patterns across s
essions and injects a short, capped, clearly-marked note at session start. Optional model-assisted p

roposal is off by default. |
| **Tool pruning** | Counts prompts where a loaded tool was never used
across sessions and proposes hiding it. Default is *propose only*; `toolprune: apply` removes the to

ol definitions from this project's model requests through DSH's own per-agent tool restriction. |
|
**Loop guard** | Detects repeated identical failures, edit churn and no-progress turns. It never sto
ps a turn; it injects at most a limited number of redirect messages and then only records/reports. O

ptional model judge is rate-limited and off if you disable it. |
| **Usage ledger** | Records the ha
rness-reported token categories (uncached input, cache read, cache write, output) and the plugin's o
wn model-call overhead. It never invents prices, currency, or savings percentages. |
## Feature status

Legend: **tested** = covered by passing offline unit tests; **verified**
= exercised end-to-end thro

ugh real DSH code paths in the offline integration
harness (`test/integration/`, real DSH packages,

fake model adapter, no paid
calls); **manual/real-model** = needs a real DSH session with your model
account, steps documented in docs/VERIFICATION.md.
| Feature | State | Notes |
| Plugin loads in a real DSH profile | verified | Tarball/link install with `dsh plugin add` into an
isolated `DSH_HOME`; composition asserted and a real `dsh` boot writes the plugin's load marker. |
| Micro-skills: env-fact families + lifecycle | tested | Upstream thresholds ported; contradictions

retire facts; cross-project state is keyed by session `cwd`. |
| Micro-skills: injection into the mo
del context | verified | Injected as an agent-scoped system-prompt section; the integration test rea

ds the first fake request's system prompt and finds the delimited note. |
| Micro-skills: model-assi
sted proposal | verified (plumbing), real model | Off by default; the digest/prompt/admission path i
s unit-tested with a fake side call, and its usage is recorded as plugin overhead. Needs a real mode

l account to judge proposal quality. |
| Tool pruning: evidence + proposal | tested | p=10 unused pr
ompts over at least 2 sessions, or at least 5 sessions regardless of length; no proposal on insuffic

ient evidence. |
[该节后续省略]
## Prerequisites

- **DSH** `0.2.1-rc.2` or later within the `0.2.x` line (declared through
`engines.dsh`). Locally ve

rified against the DSH CLI `0.2.1-rc.2` and the
desktop runtime `0.2.1-rc.3` package sources.
- **No

de.js 24+** (the DSH runtime ships Node 24; this plugin uses ESM and
`node:test`).
- **No Python req

uired.** The upstream Python plugin is not executed; its
mechanisms are reimplemented in JavaScript

in this repository.
- No API key of its own: optional model calls use the session's existing DSH
mod

el route and account, so they appear in your normal usage.
- No separate network service or telemetr

y. Optional learning and judge calls
use the current DSH model route and may consume model quota.
## Known limitations

- **Tool pruning acts at agent creation.** A session that is already running is
not re-composed mid-

turn; the change applies to the next agent/session in that
project. Explicit `/tokeneconomizer toolp

rune apply` re-registers the
restriction for the live agent but never rewrites an in-flight request.

This is
deliberate: DSH caches prompt/tool prefixes.
- **Pruned tools are hidden, not denied.** DSH

's restriction removes the
declarations from the model request; your permissions and approval policy

are
unchanged, and the tool can still be called by name if some other party emits
a call (the harne

ss answers `UNKNOWN_TOOL` when the definition is hidden).
- **User-visible "still stuck" notice**: D

SH does not expose a plugin -> user
notification channel to this plugin in headless or command-less

sessions. The
guard records the notice in state and logs it; the model-facing redirect uses
DSH stee

ring. See docs/VERIFICATION.md for the exact
test and the manual step to observe it in the TUI.
- **

Model-assisted learning is a documented simplification.** With
`microskills: on`, a digest-only mode

l proposer runs every *k* folded sessions
and accepts a claim only when its checks are supported by

at least two of the
sessions it cites. Accepted notes are injected inside a separate, clearly
marked

block and retire after three consecutive sessions without a matching
check. Upstream's full extract

or DSL and its per-task detector replay are not
ported; the deterministic `envfacts` layer is the fa

ithful part.
- **Usage is tokens, not money.** The plugin records the token categories DSH
reports.

It does not embed vendor prices, so it cannot and does not claim a
cost or a savings percentage. Mis

sing provider usage is shown as unknown.
- **Micro-skills is opt-in.** Deterministic `envfacts` lear

ning is cheap but
only helps repositories with repeated environment failures; it is off by
default l

ike upstream.
- **Loop guard cold start.** It never intervenes until it has observed the
configured

number of well-behaved turns in that project, so a fresh project
is never interrupted.
[该节后续省略]
